_readme: Escape hatch for the CI vulnerability gates (#146). An entry here mutes ONE advisory
in ONE ecosystem until a stated date, so an unfixable upstream advisory cannot block
every unrelated PR — while never becoming a permanent, forgotten hole.
Add an entry only when there is no fixed version to move to (or the fix is a breaking
major that needs its own PR — file that PR and link it in the reason).
Prefer, in order: bump the package; npm `overrides` / a direct NuGet pin to force a
patched transitive version; only then an exception.
Every field is validated; a malformed entry is IGNORED (it never suppresses)
and CI prints a warning naming the problem. Fields:
id        EXACT canonical GHSA, e.g. GHSA-93q8-gq69-wqmw (matched case-insensitively).
Only a whole GHSA is accepted — a value with extra text, a comma, or a
newline is rejected. An advisory with no GHSA (a bare CVE/other) cannot be
excepted; bump or pin the package instead.
ecosystem npm | nuget | any. REQUIRED — a missing scope is rejected, not treated as any.
reason    why it cannot be fixed now, and what unblocks it — a reviewer reads this. REQUIRED.
expires   YYYY-MM-DD. REQUIRED, and must be a real calendar date (2026-02-30 is rejected).
Inclusive through the END of that UTC day; the next day the advisory blocks
again and CI warns the entry is stale. A missing/non-ISO/impossible date never
suppresses, so an indefinite mute is impossible.
Example:
{ "id": "GHSA-93q8-gq69-wqmw", "ecosystem": "npm",
"reason": "no patched release upstream; not reachable from our code path — tracked in #999",

exceptions.reason: react-router RSC-mode CSRF; only fix is breaking major 8.3.0, no 7.x backport yet. Not reachable: SPA uses classic BrowserRouter, no RSC/server actions. Tracked in #199.
